The hand-off flag itself, `*tmp_flag = atomicInc(scratchFlag, gridDim.x);` at llmc/layernorm.cuh L378 (thread 0, relaxed atom.global.inc on scratch[0], a different address from the partials), is an atomic and not part of the racing pair; it is the attempted publication.
thread_pair_example: block A (e.g. block 0), thread t (e.g. thread 0) stores 128 bits at scratch_dbias + i + 2*C*0 (L371, with i = t * 4) after the __syncthreads at L360 and before the __syncthreads at L374; its thread 0 then does atomicInc on scratchFlag (L378). The last-arriving block B (the one whose atomicInc returned gridDim.x - 1, e.g. block 83 of 2*numSMs) thread t loads the same address at L391 (read_block_idx = 0). No __threadfence() before the atomicInc nor after observing the flag; the __syncthreads at L374/L380 are CTA-scope only.
class_reason: Both accesses are plain (non-volatile, non-atomic) 128-bit global accesses (verify.strong_accesses: none for the pair); the atomicInc flag is the attempted hand-off only (relaxed, different address). bar.sync orders threads within one CTA only and a relaxed atomic on another address does not release the earlier stores, so there is no happens-before edge from block A's stores to the last block's loads. Plain vs plain unordered = DR under D20. In practice it works because L2 atomics execute after earlier stores of the same SM drain; formally it is message passing without release/acquire.
buggy_expected: the pair (L371/L372 store128 by block A) x (L391/L392 load128 by the last block) on scratch (global) is reported as DR (cross-block RAW); a detector must model atomicInc as relaxed (not acq_rel) and must not treat bar.sync or any atomic as a GPU-scope fence

upstream_status.dispute_points: (1) On real hardware this essentially always works because atomics execute at L2 after earlier stores from the same SM have drained; a skeptic will say 'not observable'. The detector follows PTX happens-before, under which it IS a race (message-passing without release/acquire), and the author's own earlier kernel5 includes the fence. (2) The detector must model atomicInc as relaxed (not acq_rel) and not treat the CTA-level __syncthreads as a GPU-scope fence; if it treats any atomic as a full fence it will miss this. (3) Repo is archived-ish (last commit 2025-05), so no fix is expected.
